questions.question: The ratio between the area of a square and that of a circle, when the length of a side of the square is equal to that of the diameter of the circle, is: (take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the side of the square be s. Then the diameter of the circle is also s.

Area of Square : Area of Circle = s² : π × (s/2)²

Ratio = s² : (π × s²) / 4 = 1 : π/4 = 4 : π

Ratio = 4 : (22/7) = 28 : 22 = 14 : 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 : 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Side of square (s) = Diameter of circle (d)

Formula: Area of Square = s² | Area of Circle = πr² (where r = d/2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12be9e59793d18f447814a565ea7b886b7b9fcb4fa26d5d6a5a3808c1e9e97ac.png] 

Let the side of the square (s) = 14 units

⇒ Diameter of the circle (d) = 14 units

⇒ Radius of the circle (r) = d ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 units

⇒ Area of the square = s² = 14 × 14 = 196 sq. units

⇒ Area of the circle = πr² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 22 × 7 = 154 sq. units

⇒ Required Ratio = 196 : 154

⇒ Dividing both by 14: 14 : 11

**∴ The correct answer is 14 : 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circle Inscribed in a Square

When a circle is inscribed in a square, the diameter of the circle is equal to the side of the square (d = s). The ratio of areas is always 4 : π.

Square Inscribed in a Circle

When a square is inscribed in a circle, the diagonal of the square is equal to the diameter of the circle (s√2 = d). The ratio of area of circle to area of square is π : 2.

Area and Perimeter Formulas

Square Area = s², Perimeter = 4s. Circle Area = πr², Circumference = 2πr.</p

questions.question: A piece of wire 132 cm long is bent successively in the shape of an equilateral triangle, a square and a circle. Then the area will be the largest in the shape of:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a fixed perimeter (constant length of wire), the area of a closed geometric shape increases as the number of sides increases.

Comparing the given shapes: Equilateral Triangle (3 sides) **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total length of wire (Perimeter) = 132 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of Equilateral Triangle = (√3 / 4) × (side)²

Area of Square = (side)²

Area of Circle = πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea722a9345f684b8023e011b800774b3063bea4fc6707e513f3224c3b177f192.png] 

**Calculations:**

1. For Equilateral Triangle:

⇒ Side = 132 ÷ 3 = 44 cm

⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × 44 × 44 = 484√3 ≈ 484 × 1.732 ≈ 838.31 cm²

2. For Square:

⇒ Side = 132 ÷ 4 = 33 cm

⇒ Area = 33 × 33 = 1089 cm²

3. For Circle:

⇒ Circumference = 2 × (22 / 7) × r = 132

⇒ r = (132 × 7) / (2 × 22) = 21 cm

⇒ Area = (22 / 7) × 21 × 21 = 22 × 3 × 21 = 1386 cm²

Comparing the areas: 1386 cm² (Circle) > 1089 cm² (Square) > 838.31 cm² (Triangle).

**∴ The correct answer is Circle.**

**__Additional Information__**

Isoperimetric Property

Among all closed curves of a given length, the circle encloses the maximum area. This is a fundamental principle in geometry.

Area of Regular Polygon

For a regular polygon with n sides and perimeter P, Area = P² / [4 × n × tan(180°/n)]. As n increases, the area increases and approaches πr².

Square vs Rectangles

For a constant perimeter, a square has a larger area than any other rectangle. Similarly, for a constant area, the square has the smallest perimeter.</p

questions.question: If a cone is divided into two parts by drawing a plane through the midpoints of its axis, then the ratio of the volume of the 2 parts of the cone is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a solid is cut parallel to its base, the ratio of the volumes is the cube of the ratio of their corresponding heights.

Since the plane passes through the midpoint, the ratio of the height of the small cone to the original cone is 1 : 2.

Volume ratio (Small Cone : Original Cone) = (1)³ : (2)³ = 1 : 8.

Volume of the upper part = 1 unit; Volume of the lower part (frustum) = 8 − 1 = 7 units.

The ratio of the volume of the 2 parts is 1 : 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A cone divided at the midpoint of its axis (height) by a plane parallel to the base.

Let the total height of the cone be H and the base radius be R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26160ada6705ea72daeeaa49cc09984f5620a0086bb705aec9b9de6ebbb7428a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Volume of a Frustum = (1/3) × π × h × (R² + r² + R × r)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let height of small cone (h₁) = H/2

⇒ By similar triangles, radius of small cone (r) = R/2

⇒ Volume of small cone (V₁) = (1/3) × π × (R/2)² × (H/2)

⇒ V₁ = (1/3) × π × (R²/4) × (H/2) = (1/24) × π × R² × H

⇒ Volume of original cone (Vₜₒₜₐₗ) = (1/3) × π × R² × H

⇒ Volume of lower part (V₂) = Vₜₒₜₐₗ − V₁

⇒ V₂ = (1/3)πR²H − (1/24)πR²H = (7/24) × π × R² × H

⇒ Ratio = V₁ : V₂ = [(1/24)πR²H] : [(7/24)πR²H]

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Similarity Property

For any similar 3D figures, the ratio of their volumes is the cube of the ratio of their linear dimensions: V₁/V₂ = (h₁/h₂)³ = (r₁/r₂)³.

Surface Area Ratio

The ratio of the surface areas (or cross-sectional areas) of similar solids is the square of the ratio of their linear dimensions: A₁/A₂ = (h₁/h₂)².

Frustum of a Cone

The volume of a frustum of height 'h' and radii 'R' and 'r' is given by V = (πh/3)(R² + r² + Rr).</p

questions.question: Two regular polygons are such that the ratio between their number of sides is 1 : 2 and the ratio of measures of their each interior angle is 3 : 4. Then the number of sides of each polygon is:
In an isosceles triangle, the length of each equal side is twice the length of the third side. The ratio of areas of the isosceles triangle and an equilateral triangle with the same perimeter is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the third side of the isosceles triangle be x. The equal sides are 2x each.

Perimeter (P) = 2x + 2x + x = 5x. Area of Isosceles = (x/4)√(4(2x)² − x²) = (x²√15)/4.

Equilateral triangle has same perimeter P = 5x, so side s = 5x/3.

Area of Equilateral = (√3/4) × (5x/3)² = 25√3x²/36.

Ratio = [(x²√15)/4] : [25√3x²/36] = 9√15 : 25√3 = 9√5 : 25 = 36√5 : 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 36√5 : 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Equal sides of isosceles triangle = 2 × Base. Perimeter of isosceles triangle = Perimeter of equilateral triangle.

Let the base of the isosceles triangle be b.

⇒ Equal sides (a) = 2b.

⇒ Perimeter of isosceles triangle = a + a + b = 2b + 2b + b = 5b.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f98a19a116d8dadcbce59b6e2372147ecfbf06f3e2befa88112c83d941e2f97d.png] 

Area of Isosceles triangle = (b/4) × √(4a² − b²)

⇒ Areaᵢₛₒ = (b/4) × √(4(2b)² − b²) = (b/4) × √(16b² − b²) = (b/4) × √15b² = (b²√15)/4.

Side of equilateral triangle (s) = Perimeter/3 = 5b/3.

Area of Equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × s²

⇒ Areaₑqᵤᵢ = (√3/4) × (5b/3)² = (√3/4) × (25b²/9) = (25√3b²)/36.

Ratio of areas = [(b²√15)/4] : [(25√3b²)/36]

⇒ Ratio = (√15/4) : (25√3/36)

⇒ Ratio = (9√15) : (25√3)

⇒ Ratio = (9 × √5 × √3) : (25 × √3)

⇒ Ratio = 9√5 : 25

To match the options, multiply both sides by 4:

⇒ Ratio = (9√5 × 4) : (25 × 4) = 36√5 : 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 36√5 : 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Isosceles Triangle

For an isosceles triangle with equal sides 'a' and base 'b', the altitude h = √(a² − (b/2)²) and Area = (b/4)√(4a² − b²).

Area of Equilateral Triangle

For an equilateral triangle with side 's', all sides are equal and all angles are 60°. Area = (√3/4)s² and height h = (√3/2)s.

Heron's Formula

Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s = (a + b + c)/2 is the semi-perimeter and a, b, c are the lengths of the sides.</p

questions.question: A right circular cylinder is partially filled with water. Two iron spherical balls are completely immersed in the water so that the height of the water in the cylinder rises by 4 cm. If the radius of one ball is half of the other and the diameter of the cylinder is 18 cm, then the radii of the spherical balls are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of water rise in cylinder = Total volume of two immersed spheres.

π × R² × h = (4/3) π × (r₁³ + r₂³)

Let radii be r and 2r. Cylinder Radius R = 18/2 = 9 cm, Height rise h = 4 cm.

9² × 4 = (4/3) × (r³ + (2r)³) ⇒ 81 × 4 = (4/3) × 9r³

324 = 12r³ ⇒ r³ = 27 ⇒ r = 3 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 cm and 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of cylinder = 18 cm ⇒ Radius (R) = 9 cm

Rise in water height (h) = 4 cm

Let radius of smaller ball = r cm

Radius of larger ball = 2r cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab0a322655a4a1d16bbe8ab848aaed942b5c1ea7ba7e9230cc46073a3f7bc24d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of cylinder = πR²h

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of water displaced = Volume of ball 1 + Volume of ball 2

⇒ π × (9)² × 4 = (4/3) × π × (r)³ + (4/3) × π × (2r)³

⇒ 81 × 4 = (4/3) × [r³ + 8r³]

⇒ 324 = (4/3) × 9r³

⇒ 324 = 12r³

⇒ r³ = 324 ÷ 12

⇒ r³ = 27

⇒ r = 3 cm

⇒ Larger radius = 2r = 2 × 3 = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3 cm and 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Archimedes Principle

An object immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces. In terms of volume, the volume of displaced liquid equals the volume of the submerged portion of the object.

Volume of Hollow Cylinder

The volume of a hollow cylinder with external radius R and internal radius r is given by V = πh(R² − r²).

Surface Area of Sphere

The surface area of a sphere of radius r is 4πr², while its volume is (4/3)πr³.</p

questions.question: The whole surface area of a pyramid whose base is a regular polygon is 340 cm² and area of its base is 100 cm². Area of each lateral face is 30 cm². Then the number of lateral faces is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Lateral Surface Area = Total Surface Area − Base Area

Lateral Surface Area = 340 − 100 = 240 cm²

Number of lateral faces = Total Lateral Area ÷ Area of each face

Number of lateral faces = 240 ÷ 30 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 340 cm²

Area of base = 100 cm²

Area of one lateral face = 30 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of Pyramid = Area of Base + (Number of faces × Area of each lateral face)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/258a898911d4f6b2e59f51725b849b8ed60ce55689eb27894147dca7a9deca4c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = TSA − Base Area

⇒ LSA = 340 − 100

⇒ LSA = 240 cm²

⇒ Let n be the number of lateral faces.

⇒ n × Area of each lateral face = LSA

⇒ n × 30 = 240

⇒ n = 240 ÷ 30

⇒ n = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Pyramid

For any pyramid, the Total Surface Area (TSA) is the sum of the base area and the lateral surface area (sum of all triangular face areas).

Lateral Surface Area of Regular Pyramid

LSA = ½ × Perimeter of base × Slant Height (l). This applies when all lateral faces are congruent triangles.

Volume of a Pyramid

Volume = 1/3 × Base Area × Vertical Height (h). It is always one-third the volume of a prism with the same base and height.</p

questions.question: If P = 99, then the value of P(P² + 3P + 3) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression P(P² + 3P + 3) can be written as P³ + 3P² + 3P.

Using the algebraic identity (a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³, we see that:

(P + 1)³ − 1 = P³ + 3P² + 3P + 1 − 1 = P³ + 3P² + 3P.

Substitute P = 99: (99 + 1)³ − 1 = 100³ − 1 = 1,000,000 − 1 = 999,999.

**∴ The correct answer is 999999.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** P = 99

**Formula Used:** (a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³

**Calculations:**

Required value = P(P² + 3P + 3)

⇒ P³ + 3P² + 3P

⇒ (P³ + 3P² + 3P + 1) − 1

⇒ (P + 1)³ − 1

⇒ (99 + 1)³ − 1

⇒ (100)³ − 1

⇒ 1000000 − 1

⇒ 999999

**∴ The correct answer is 999999.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube of a Sum Identity

(a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³. In this problem, putting b = 1 gives a³ + 3a² + 3a + 1.

Cube of a Difference Identity

(a − b)³ = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³. For b = 1, it results in a³ − 3a² + 3a − 1.

Sum and Difference of Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).</p

questions.question: If x + 1/x = c + 1/c then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The equation x + 1/x = c + 1/c is symmetric with respect to x and c.

By inspection, if we substitute x = c, both sides become identical (c + 1/c = c + 1/c).

In reciprocal equations of the form f(x) + 1/f(x) = k, if x is a root, then 1/x is also a root.

By substituting x = 1/c, the equation becomes 1/c + c = c + 1/c, which is also true.

Thus, the two values satisfying the equation are c and its reciprocal 1/c.

**∴ The correct answer is c, 1/c.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x + 1/x = c + 1/c

**Formula Used:** Quadratic rearrangement and factorisation.

⇒ x − c + 1/x − 1/c = 0

⇒ (x − c) + (c − x) / (cx) = 0

⇒ (x − c) − (x − c) / (cx) = 0

⇒ (x − c) [1 − 1/(cx)] = 0

⇒ (x − c) [(cx − 1) / (cx)] = 0

⇒ x − c = 0 or cx − 1 = 0

⇒ x = c or x = 1/c

**∴ The correct answer is c, 1/c.**

**__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Equations

Equations where the reciprocal of any root is also a root of the equation. These often take the form x + 1/x = k.

Product of Roots in Reciprocal Form

The equation x + 1/x = a can be written as x² − ax + 1 = 0. According to Vieta's formulas, the product of roots (c/a) is 1/1 = 1.

Nature of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots are real and distinct if the discriminant D = b² − 4ac > 0.</p

questions.question: If the sum of squares of two real numbers is 41 and their sum is 9. Then the sum of cubes of these two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Test integer pairs whose sum is 9: (1,8), (2,7), (3,6), (4,5).

Check squares: 4² + 5² = 16 + 25 = 41. (Condition satisfied)

Sum of cubes: 4³ + 5³ = 64 + 125 = 189.

**∴ The correct answer is 189.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Sum of numbers (x + y) = 9

Sum of squares (x² + y²) = 41

Formula used: (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

Formula used: x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² + y² − xy)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/220c80bbb7fadd52e296e9c2f1b9f65476f8bb0ec0089b4b27870cc8a5f3683d.png] 

⇒ (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

⇒ 9² = 41 + 2xy

⇒ 81 = 41 + 2xy

⇒ 2xy = 81 − 41 = 40

⇒ xy = 20

⇒ x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² + y² − xy)

⇒ x³ + y³ = 9 × (41 − 20)

⇒ x³ + y³ = 9 × 21 = 189

**∴ The correct answer is 189.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

The sum of cubes can also be written as: x³ + y³ = (x + y)³ − 3xy(x + y).

Difference of Cubes

The identity for the difference of two cubes is: x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²).

Product of Numbers

Given the sum and sum of squares, the product of two numbers is always xy = [(x + y)² − (x² + y²)] ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: A complete factorisation of x⁴ + 64 is:
If a + b = 1, then a⁴ + b⁴ – a³ – b³ – 2a²b² + ab is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For algebraic identities given with a condition like a + b = 1, use the value substitution method.

Let a = 1 and b = 0, which satisfies the condition 1 + 0 = 1.

Substitute these values into the expression: 1⁴ + 0⁴ − 1³ − 0³ − 2(1² × 0²) + (1 × 0)

⇒ 1 + 0 − 1 − 0 − 0 + 0 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: a + b = 1

Expression: a⁴ + b⁴ − a³ − b³ − 2a²b² + ab

Step 1: Rearrange and group the terms.

⇒ (a⁴ + b⁴ − 2a²b²) − (a³ + b³) + ab

Step 2: Apply the identity (x² − y²)² = x⁴ + y⁴ − 2x²y² and the sum of cubes identity.

⇒ (a² − b²)² − (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) + ab

Step 3: Since a + b = 1, substitute this value into the expression.

⇒ [(a + b)(a − b)]² − (1)(a² − ab + b²) + ab

⇒ (1 × (a − b))² − a² + ab − b² + ab

⇒ (a − b)² − a² + 2ab − b²

Step 4: Expand (a − b)².

⇒ (a² − 2ab + b²) − a² + 2ab − b²

⇒ 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum and Difference of Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Basic Algebraic Identities

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

Value Substitution Method

In competitive exams, if an expression is true for a given condition, substituting simple values (like 0, 1, −1) that satisfy the condition often yields the answer quickly.</p

questions.question: If x² + y² + 6x + 5 = 4(x – y) then x – y is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify perfect squares by rearranging: x² + 2x + 1 + y² + 4y + 4 = 0.

The equation simplifies to: (x + 1)² + (y + 2)² = 0.

For the sum of squares of real numbers to be zero, each square must be zero.

∴ x + 1 = 0 → x = −1 and y + 2 = 0 → y = −2.

Then, x − y = −1 − (−2) = −1 + 2 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: x² + y² + 6x + 5 = 4(x − y)

Formula used: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

⇒ x² + y² + 6x + 5 = 4x − 4y

⇒ x² + 6x − 4x + y² + 4y + 5 = 0

⇒ x² + 2x + y² + 4y + 5 = 0

⇒ (x² + 2x + 1) + (y² + 4y + 4) = 0

⇒ (x + 1)² + (y + 2)² = 0

Since the sum of squares is zero, each base must be zero independently:

⇒ x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = −1

⇒ y + 2 = 0 ⇒ y = −2

⇒ x − y = (−1) − (−2) = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Property

If a² + b² + c² + ... = 0 for real numbers, then a = b = c = ... = 0.

Perfect Square Identities

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² are fundamental in completing the square.

Quadratic Expressions

To complete the square for x² + kx, add and subtract (k/2)².</p

questions.question: If a = 299, b = 298, c = 297 then the value of 2a³ + 2b³ + 2c³ – 6abc is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If numbers a, b, and c are in Arithmetic Progression (AP) with common difference d, then a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 9 × middle term × d².

Here a = 299, b = 298, c = 297 are in AP with middle term b = 298 and common difference d = 1.

The given expression is 2 × (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc).

Value = 2 × (9 × 298 × 1²) = 18 × 298 = 5364.

**∴ The correct answer is 5364.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: a = 299, b = 298, c = 297

Formula used: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = ½(a + b + c)[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]

⇒ Required expression = 2a³ + 2b³ + 2c³ − 6abc = 2(a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc)

⇒ Value = 2 × ½ × (a + b + c)[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]

⇒ Value = (a + b + c)[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]

⇒ Sum (a + b + c) = 299 + 298 + 297 = 894

⇒ Differences: (a − b) = 1, (b − c) = 1, (c − a) = −2

⇒ Value = 894 × [1² + 1² + (−2)²]

⇒ Value = 894 × [1 + 1 + 4] = 894 × 6

⇒ Value = 5364

**∴ The correct answer is 5364.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Algebraic Identity

The expansion of a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc is (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca).

Sum of Squares Relation

The term (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) can also be written as ½[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²].

Special Conditional Property

If (a + b + c) = 0 or if a = b = c, then the value of a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 0, which implies a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.</p

questions.question: If x + 1/x = √3, then the value of x¹⁸ + x¹² + x⁶ + 1 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If x + 1/x = √3, then the property x⁶ = −1 (or x⁶ + 1 = 0) is always satisfied.

For any two terms xⁿ and xm where the difference between powers |n − m| = 6, their sum is 0.

The given expression is x¹⁸ + x¹² + x⁶ + 1.

Grouping the terms: (x¹⁸ + x¹²) + (x⁶ + 1) = x¹²(x⁶ + 1) + (x⁶ + 1).

Substituting x⁶ + 1 = 0: (x¹² × 0) + 0 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: x + 1/x = √3

Formula Used: (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ Cubing both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (x + 1/x)³ = (√3)³

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + 3 × x × (1/x) × (x + 1/x) = 3√3

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + 3 × (√3) = 3√3

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 3√3 − 3√3 = 0

⇒ (x⁶ + 1) / x³ = 0 ⇒ x⁶ + 1 = 0 ⇒ x⁶ = −1

⇒ Now, substitute x⁶ = −1 in the expression x¹⁸ + x¹² + x⁶ + 1:

⇒ (x⁶)³ + (x⁶)² + (x⁶)¹ + 1

⇒ (−1)³ + (−1)² + (−1) + 1

⇒ −1 + 1 − 1 + 1 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

**__Additional Information__**

Special Case: x + 1/x = 1

If x + 1/x = 1, then x³ + 1 = 0, which implies x³ = −1.

Special Case: x + 1/x = −1

If x + 1/x = −1, then x³ − 1 = 0, which implies x³ = 1.

Special Case: x + 1/x = √2

If x + 1/x = √2, then x⁴ + 1 = 0, which implies x⁴ = −1.

General Result for √3

When x + 1/x = √3, any expression of the form xⁿ + xⁿ⁻⁶ + xm + xm⁻⁶ + ... will always result in 0.</p

questions.question: If x = 1 + √2 + √3, then the value of 2x⁴ – 8x³ – 5x² + 26x – 28 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rearrange x = 1 + √2 + √3 to (x − 1)² = (√2 + √3)² ⇒ x² − 2x − 4 = 2√6.

Square again: (x² − 2x − 4)² = 24 ⇒ x⁴ − 4x³ − 4x² + 16x − 8 = 0.

Multiply by 2: 2x⁴ − 8x³ − 8x² + 32x − 16 = 0.

Target expression = (2x⁴ − 8x³ − 8x² + 32x − 16) + 3(x² − 2x − 4).

Substitute values: 0 + 3(2√6) = 6√6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6√6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x = 1 + √2 + √3

**Formula:** (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca

⇒ x − 1 = √2 + √3

⇒ (x − 1)² = (√2 + √3)²

⇒ x² − 2x + 1 = 2 + 3 + 2√6

⇒ x² − 2x − 4 = 2√6

⇒ (x² − 2x − 4)² = (2√6)²

⇒ x⁴ + 4x² + 16 + 2(x²)(−2x) + 2(−2x)(−4) + 2(x²)(−4) = 24

⇒ x⁴ + 4x² + 16 − 4x³ + 16x − 8x² = 24

⇒ x⁴ − 4x³ − 4x² + 16x − 8 = 0

Now, rewrite the given expression: 2x⁴ − 8x³ − 5x² + 26x − 28

⇒ 2(x⁴ − 4x³ − 4x² + 16x − 8) + 8x² − 32x + 16 − 5x² + 26x − 28

⇒ 2(0) + 3x² − 6x − 12

⇒ 3(x² − 2x − 4)

⇒ 3 × 2√6 = 6√6

**∴ The correct answer is 6√6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Expansion of (a + b + c)² is a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca. This is vital for solving equations with multiple radicals.

Rationalization and Polynomials

If a variable equals a sum of surds, repeated squaring can transform it into a polynomial with integer coefficients equal to zero.

Remainder Theorem

For any polynomial P(x), if we find a divisor D(x) such that D(x) = 0, then the value of P(x) is simply the remainder R(x) when P(x) is divided by D(x).</p

questions.question: If 2r=h+sqrt{{{r}²}+{{h}²}} then the ratio r : h (r ≠ 0) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Test the ratio options directly in the equation 2r − h = √(r² + h²).

For Option (3) 4 : 3, let r = 4 and h = 3.

LHS = 2(4) − 3 = 8 − 3 = 5.

RHS = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5.

Since LHS = RHS, the ratio r : h = 4 : 3 is the correct solution.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: 2r = h + √(r² + h²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d1d5c54d50fa8e9b9c1e8f8be8a4bbd810fabcddf37492e4fba3d104dd0b1318.png] 

⇒ 2r − h = √(r² + h²)

Squaring both sides:

⇒ (2r − h)² = (√(r² + h²))²

⇒ 4r² + h² − 4rh = r² + h²

⇒ 4r² − r² = 4rh

⇒ 3r² = 4rh

Dividing both sides by rh (since r ≠ 0 and h ≠ 0):

⇒ 3r/h = 4

⇒ r/h = 4/3

⇒ r : h = 4 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab. This is used to expand terms when solving equations involving radicals.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers a, b, and c such that a² + b² = c². Examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Ratio and Proportion

If x/y = a/b, then x : y = a : b. Ratios represent the relative size of two quantities and are independent of actual units.</p

questions.question: In an equilateral triangle ABC, G is the centroid. Each side of the triangle is 6 cm. The length of AG is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In an equilateral triangle, the distance from the vertex to the centroid (AG) is equal to the circumradius (R).

Shortcut Formula: AG = side / √3

Given: side = 6 cm

⇒ AG = 6 / √3 = (2 × 3) / √3 = 2√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of equilateral triangle ABC (a) = 6 cm

G = Centroid of the triangle

**Formula Used:**

Height (h) of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 2) × a

Distance from vertex to centroid (AG) = (2/3) × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a664775e1e3c3258150103834b9135c0e9ae011baa4d96be3b6e33db959a0278.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Height (AD) = (√3 / 2) × 6

⇒ AD = 3√3 cm

⇒ In an equilateral triangle, the centroid G divides the altitude AD in the ratio 2 : 1.

⇒ AG = (2 / 3) × AD

⇒ AG = (2 / 3) × 3√3

⇒ AG = 2√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Height and Area of Equilateral Triangle

The height (h) is given by (√3/2) × a and the area is given by (√3/4) × a², where 'a' is the side.

Circumradius and Inradius

For an equilateral triangle, the circumradius (R) is a/√3 and the inradius (r) is a/(2√3). Note that R = 2r.

Centroid Property

The centroid G of any triangle divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex to the base.</p

questions.question: PQ is a tangent to the circle at T. If TR = TS where, R and S are points on the circle and ∠RST = 65°, the ∠PTS = ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In ΔTRS, given TR = TS and ∠RST = 65°, so ∠TRS = ∠RST = 65°.

By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between the tangent QT and chord TS is equal to the angle in the alternate segment, ∠TRS.

⇒ ∠QTS = ∠TRS = 65°.

Since PQ is a straight line tangent at T, ∠PTS = 180° − ∠QTS = 180° − 65° = 115°.

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠RST = 65°, TR = TS, PQ is a tangent at T.

**Formula Used:** Alternate Segment Theorem; Angle sum property of triangle; Angles opposite to equal sides in a triangle are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/972e7a5e7ccd6f40458cdfba583f638beadf187d89479a9e564578c90780ae72.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ In ΔTRS, TR = TS (Given)

⇒ ∠TRS = ∠TSR = 65° (Angles opposite to equal sides are equal)

⇒ In ΔTRS, ∠RTS + ∠TRS + ∠TSR = 180° (Angle sum property)

⇒ ∠RTS + 65° + 65° = 180°

⇒ ∠RTS = 180° − 130° = 50°

⇒ According to the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between tangent PT and chord TR is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠PTR = ∠TSR = 65°

⇒ ∠PTS = ∠PTR + ∠RTS

⇒ ∠PTS = 65° + 50° = 115°

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a chord and a tangent through one of the end points of the chord is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

Isosceles Triangle Property

In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are always equal in measure.

Tangents to a Circle

A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. From an external point, exactly two tangents can be drawn to a circle, and they are equal in length.</p

questions.question: In ΔABC, AC = BC and ∠ABC = 50°, the side BC is produced to D so that BC = CD then the value of ∠BAD is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given $AC = BC$ and $BC = CD$, we have $AC = BC = CD$.

This implies point $C$ is equidistant from points $A, B,$ and $D$.

Thus, $C$ is the circumcenter of $\triangle ABD$, making $BD$ the diameter of its circumcircle.

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always $90°$.

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** $AC = BC$, $\angle ABC = 50°$, and $BC = CD$.

**Formula Used:** Angle sum property of a triangle and Isosceles triangle property (angles opposite to equal sides are equal).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/411bdbc03d49be3ffa3426e5294bf77354e1d3f5a0ceb06ee0701c430187f044.png] 

⇒ In $\triangle ABC$, $AC = BC$ ⇒ $\angle BAC = \angle ABC = 50°$.

⇒ In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 180° − (\angle BAC + \angle ABC) = 180° − (50° + 50°) = 80°$.

⇒ Since $BCD$ is a straight line, $\angle ACD = 180° − \angle ACB = 180° − 80° = 100°$.

⇒ Given $BC = CD$ and $AC = BC$ ⇒ $AC = CD$.

⇒ In $\triangle ACD$, $AC = CD$ ⇒ $\angle CAD = \angle CDA = (180° − 100°) \div 2 = 40°$.

⇒ $\angle BAD = \angle BAC + \angle CAD = 50° + 40° = 90°$.

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Theorem

If two sides of a triangle are equal, then the angles opposite to those sides are also equal.

Angle in a Semicircle

According to Thales's Theorem, the angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of a circle is always $90°$.

Exterior Angle Property

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two interior opposite angles.</p

questions.question: In a circle, a diameter AB and a chord PQ (which is not a diameter) intersect each other at X perpendicularly. If AX : BX = 3 : 2 and the radius of the circle is 5 cm, then the length of chord PQ is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Radius = 5 cm → Diameter AB = 10 cm.

Divide AB in ratio 3 : 2 ⇒ AX = 6 cm and BX = 4 cm.

Since diameter AB is perpendicular to chord PQ, X is the midpoint of PQ.

By Intersecting Chords Theorem: (PQ/2)² = AX × BX.

(PQ/2)² = 6 × 4 = 24 ⇒ PQ/2 = √24 = 2√6.

PQ = 2 × 2√6 = 4√6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4√6 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c707ac19635c24e82699a6d1e5edec5ffd79b86a2684233ec89af15342328a2.png] 

Given:

Radius (r) = 5 cm ⇒ Diameter (AB) = 10 cm.

Ratio AX : BX = 3 : 2.

Formula used:

1. Intersecting Chords Theorem: AX × BX = PX × XQ.

2. A radius perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord: PX = XQ.

Calculations:

⇒ Total length of diameter AB = 10 cm.

⇒ AX = (3 / (3 + 2)) × 10 = (3/5) × 10 = 6 cm.

⇒ BX = (2 / (3 + 2)) × 10 = (2/5) × 10 = 4 cm.

⇒ Since AB ⊥ PQ, X is the midpoint of PQ ⇒ PX = XQ.

⇒ PX × XQ = AX × BX

⇒ PX² = 6 × 4 = 24

⇒ PX = √24 = 2√6 cm.

⇒ Length of chord PQ = PX + XQ = 2 × PX = 2 × 2√6 = 4√6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4√6 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Intersecting Chords Theorem

When two chords AB and PQ intersect at point X inside a circle, then AX × BX = PX × XQ.

Perpendicular Bisector Property

A line drawn from the center of a circle perpendicular to a chord always bisects that chord into two equal segments.

Pythagoras in Circles

For a chord of length L at distance d from the center of a circle with radius r, the relation is r² = d² + (L/2)².</p

questions.question: ABC is a triangle, PQ is line segment intersecting AB in P and AC in Q and PQ II BC. The ratio of AP : BP = 3 : 5 and length of PQ is 18 cm. The length of BC is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In ▵ABC, since PQ || BC, ▵APQ ∼ ▵ABC.

The ratio of sides is AP : AB = AP : (AP + BP) = 3 : (3 + 5) = 3 : 8.

By similarity, PQ ÷ BC = AP ÷ AB.

18 ÷ BC = 3 ÷ 8.

BC = (18 × 8) ÷ 3 = 6 × 8 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: In ▵ABC, PQ || BC. AP : BP = 3 : 5 and PQ = 18 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db336048e0e5326c17c55ea01a4644a7da023cb1ac932d84afbe0c7340f0c40d.png] 

Formula: If PQ || BC, then ▵APQ ∼ ▵ABC (AA similarity).

⇒ AP ÷ AB = PQ ÷ BC

⇒ AB = AP + BP

⇒ AB = 3 + 5 = 8 units (Letting AP = 3 units and BP = 5 units)

⇒ 3 ÷ 8 = 18 ÷ BC

⇒ 3 × BC = 18 × 8

⇒ BC = 144 ÷ 3

⇒ BC = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: AP ÷ PB = AQ ÷ QC.

Ratio of Areas of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(▵APQ) ÷ Area(▵ABC) = (AP ÷ AB)².

Midpoint Theorem

If P and Q are the midpoints of AB and AC respectively, then PQ is parallel to BC and PQ = 1 ÷ 2 × BC.</p

questions.question: If the parallel sides of a trapezium are 8 cm and 4 cm, M and N are the midpoints of the diagonals of the trapezium, then the length of MN is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The length of the line segment joining the midpoints of the diagonals of a trapezium is half the difference of its parallel sides.

Length MN = (Longer parallel side − Shorter parallel side) ÷ 2

MN = (8 cm − 4 cm) ÷ 2

MN = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Parallel sides AB = 8 cm and CD = 4 cm. M and N are midpoints of diagonals AC and BD.

**Formula:** Length of the line joining midpoints of diagonals = (Difference of parallel sides) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92381459c9b00610d09f7d058b10c1a3c4f4c5be016c8351d72b8e3e631ba0c9.png] 

⇒ Parallel side 1 (a) = 8 cm

⇒ Parallel side 2 (b) = 4 cm

⇒ Length MN = (a − b) ÷ 2

⇒ MN = (8 − 4) ÷ 2

⇒ MN = 4 ÷ 2

⇒ MN = 2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides is called the median and its length is equal to (a + b) ÷ 2.

Area of a Trapezium

The area is calculated as Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height.

Property of Diagonals

In a trapezium, the diagonals divide each other in the same ratio as the ratio of the parallel sides.</p

questions.question: ΔABC is isosceles having AB = AC and ∠A = 40°. Bisectors PO and OQ of the exterior angles ∠ABD and ∠ACE formed by producing BC on both sides, meet at O. The value of ∠BOC is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The point O is the ex-center of ΔABC opposite to vertex A.

The angle formed by the exterior angle bisectors is given by the formula: ∠BOC = 90° − (∠A ÷ 2)

Given ∠A = 40°

∠BOC = 90° − (40° ÷ 2) = 90° − 20° = 70°.

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AB = AC, ∠A = 40°, BO and CO are exterior angle bisectors.

In ΔABC, sum of angles = 180°

⇒ ∠A + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

Since AB = AC, ∠ABC = ∠ACB

⇒ 40° + 2 × ∠ABC = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠ABC = 140° ⇒ ∠ABC = 70° and ∠ACB = 70°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65a1230f66899a617ddd70335a209324e6f21da62e7ef08ca3e9631ac5d0d8e6.png] 

Exterior ∠ABD = 180° − ∠ABC = 180° − 70° = 110°

Exterior ∠ACE = 180° − ∠ACB = 180° − 70° = 110°

Since BO and CO are bisectors:

⇒ ∠OBC = ∠ABD ÷ 2 = 110° ÷ 2 = 55°

⇒ ∠OCB = ∠ACE ÷ 2 = 110° ÷ 2 = 55°

In ΔBOC:

⇒ ∠BOC + ∠OBC + ∠OCB = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC + 55° + 55° = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC + 110° = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC = 180° − 110° = 70°

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Interior Angle Bisector

The angle formed by the intersection of internal bisectors of ∠B and ∠C is 90° + ∠A/2.

Ex-center Property

The intersection of two exterior angle bisectors and one interior angle bisector (from the third vertex) is called the ex-center.

Sum of External Bisectors

The angle between internal bisector and external bisector of the same vertex is always 90°.</p

questions.question: An equilateral triangle of side 6 cm is inscribed in a circle,then the radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For an equilateral triangle of side 'a', the circumradius (R) is calculated as R = a ÷ √3.

Given side a = 6 cm.

R = 6 ÷ √3 = (2 × 3) ÷ √3 = 2√3 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Side of equilateral triangle (a) = 6 cm.

Formula Used: Radius of the circumcircle (R) = Side / √3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5da475450d83916544be02d813764afa43957779f38990597c60ba78245640da.png] 

⇒ Circumradius (R) = 6 / √3

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator: R = (6 × √3) / (√3 × √3)

⇒ R = 6√3 / 3

⇒ R = 2√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inradius of Equilateral Triangle

The radius of the inscribed circle (inradius) is r = a / (2√3). The circumradius R is always twice the inradius (R = 2r).

Height of Equilateral Triangle

The height (h) is given by h = (√3/2) × a. The circumradius (R) is also equal to 2/3 of the height (R = 2/3 × h).

Area of Equilateral Triangle

The area is calculated as A = (√3/4) × a², where 'a' is the length of the side.</p

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AB is diameter and CD is a chord which is equal to the radius OC. AC and BD are extended in such a way that they intersect each other at a point P, exterior to the circle. The measure of ∠APB is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Measure of Arc AB = 180° (since AB is the diameter).

Chord CD = Radius ⇒ ∠COD = 60° ⇒ Measure of Arc CD = 60°.

Angle formed by two secants intersecting outside = (Major Arc − Minor Arc) ÷ 2.

∠APB = (Arc AB − Arc CD) ÷ 2 = (180° − 60°) ÷ 2 = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** O is the centre, AB is the diameter, and chord CD = radius OC = OD.

**Formula:** Angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended at the circumference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2612c6927aa632f3858eb1fe6e8c49b1ec8b9f8f37bb9721ea5a266f9ac67b2c.png] 

⇒ In ▵COD, OC = OD = CD (all are equal to radius).

⇒ ∴ ▵COD is an equilateral triangle ⇒ ∠COD = 60°.

⇒ Angle at circumference ∠CAD = ∠COD ÷ 2 = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°.

⇒ ∠ADB = 90° (Angle subtended by diameter AB in a semi-circle).

⇒ In ▵PAD, ∠ADB is an exterior angle to the triangle.

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠PAD + ∠APD

⇒ 90° = 30° + ∠APB

⇒ ∠APB = 90° − 30° = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semi-circle

An angle subtended by the diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Central Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is twice the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Intersecting Secants Theorem

The angle formed by two secants intersecting outside a circle is half the positive difference of the measures of the intercepted arcs: ∠P = (Arc₁ − Arc₂) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: Two chords AB and CD of a circle with centre O intersect at P. If ∠APC = 40°,then the value of ∠AOC + ∠BOD is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle between two intersecting chords inside a circle is half the sum of the angles subtended by the intercepted arcs at the center.

Angle between chords (∠APC) = (∠AOC + ∠BOD) ÷ 2

Given ∠APC = 40°

⇒ 40° = (∠AOC + ∠BOD) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠AOC + ∠BOD = 40° × 2 = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Chords AB and CD intersect at P. O is the center. ∠APC = 40°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73ce2646b7e9e14f22f8268930d8870b6734750cf7ba56c0a95e9c077afe9559.png] 

Join AD. In ▵APD:

⇒ ∠APC is the exterior angle to ▵APD.

⇒ ∠APC = ∠PAD + ∠PDA

⇒ ∠PAD is the angle subtended by arc BD at the circumference, so ∠PAD = ∠BOD ÷ 2

⇒ ∠PDA is the angle subtended by arc AC at the circumference, so ∠PDA = ∠AOC ÷ 2

Substituting these in the exterior angle equation:

⇒ ∠APC = (∠BOD ÷ 2) + (∠AOC ÷ 2)

⇒ 40° = (∠BOD + ∠AOC) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠AOC + ∠BOD = 40° × 2

⇒ ∠AOC + ∠BOD = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Central Angle Property

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is twice the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the circumference.

Interior Intersecting Chords

When two chords intersect inside a circle, the measure of the angle formed is half the sum of the measures of the intercepted arcs.

Exterior Intersecting Chords

If two chords intersect outside the circle, the angle formed is half the difference of the intercepted arcs.

Power of a Point

For chords AB and CD intersecting at P, the product of segments of the chords is equal: AP × PB = CP × PD.</p

questions.question: If x tan 60° + cos 45° = sec 45° then the value of x² + 1 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Substitute tan 60° = √3, cos 45° = 1/√2 and sec 45° = √2.

x × √3 + 1/√2 = √2

x√3 = √2 − 1/√2 = 1/√2

x = 1/√6 ⇒ x² = 1/6

x² + 1 = 1/6 + 1 = 7/6

**∴ The correct answer is 7/6.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x tan 60° + cos 45° = sec 45°

**Formula Used:** Standard trigonometric values: tan 60° = √3, cos 45° = 1/√2, sec 45° = √2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50c1dd10439ad3ab6c3eec60d04c8af2815e2267c44a4f6fb7601cbedf28777.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x(√3) + 1/√2 = √2

⇒ x√3 = √2 − 1/√2

⇒ x√3 = (2 − 1) / √2

⇒ x√3 = 1/√2

⇒ x = 1 / (√3 × √2)

⇒ x = 1 / √6

⇒ x² = (1/√6)² = 1/6

⇒ x² + 1 = 1/6 + 1

⇒ x² + 1 = 7/6

**∴ The correct answer is 7/6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Table Values

Values for 45°: sin 45° = 1/√2, cos 45° = 1/√2, tan 45° = 1. Values for 60°: sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3.

Reciprocal Identities

Secant is the reciprocal of cosine: sec θ = 1/cos θ. Similarly, cosec θ = 1/sin θ and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental relations: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.</p

Complementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin θ = cos(90° − θ), tan θ = cot(90° − θ), and sec θ = csc(90° − θ). These are used when the sum of angles is 90°.

Standard Trigonometric Values of Tangent

questions.question: If a²sec²x - b²tan²x = c² then the value of sec²x + tan²x is equal to (assume b² ≠ a²)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume a simple value for x, let x = 0°.

Then sec²0 = 1 and tan²0 = 0.

Substitute in the equation: a²(1) − b²(0) = c² ⇒ a² = c².

The target value to find is: sec²0 + tan²0 = 1 + 0 = 1.

Check Option 2 with a² = c²: (b² + a² − 2a²) / (b² − a²) = (b² − a²) / (b² − a²) = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is (b² + a² − 2c²) / (b² − a²).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** a²sec²x − b²tan²x = c²

**Formula used:** sec²x = 1 + tan²x

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bdc184253672a55d2d4960c615aad62a087010519450066b5ea727d06382239c.png] 

⇒ a²(1 + tan²x) − b²tan²x = c²

⇒ a² + a² tan²x − b² tan²x = c²

⇒ tan²x(a² − b²) = c² − a²

⇒ tan²x = (c² − a²) / (a² − b²)

⇒ sec²x = 1 + tan²x = 1 + (c² − a²) / (a² − b²)

⇒ sec²x = (a² − b² + c² − a²) / (a² − b²) = (c² − b²) / (a² − b²)

⇒ sec²x + tan²x = [ (c² − b²) + (c² − a²) ] / (a² − b²)

⇒ sec²x + tan²x = (2c² − a² − b²) / (a² − b²)

⇒ Multiplying numerator and denominator by −1: (a² + b² − 2c²) / (b² − a²)

**∴ The correct answer is (b² + a² − 2c²) / (b² − a²).**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²x + cos²x = 1, sec²x − tan²x = 1, and csc²x − cot²x = 1.

Substitution Method

For trigonometric expressions, substituting standard angles like 0°, 30°, or 45° can often simplify complex algebraic relations and verify options quickly.

Double Angle Formulas

cos 2x = cos²x − sin²x = 1 − 2sin²x = 2cos²x − 1 = (1 − tan²x) / (1 + tan²x).</p

questions.question: (1 + sec 20° + cot 70°)(1 - cosec 20° + tan70°) is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert angles to 20° using complementary rules: cot 70° = tan 20° and tan 70° = cot 20°.

The expression simplifies to: (1 + tan 20° + sec 20°)(1 + cot 20° − cosec 20°).

Recognize the standard trigonometric identity: (1 + tan θ + sec θ)(1 + cot θ − cosec θ) = 2.

This result is independent of the value of θ.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (1 + sec 20° + cot 70°)(1 − cosec 20° + tan 70°)

**Formula Used:** tan(90° − θ) = cot θ; cot(90° − θ) = tan θ; sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0538100faf2aabc577d7db8ab66f6f0dcdd105256571948f19dc142a3e106c6.png] 

⇒ Convert 70° to 20°: cot 70° = tan 20° and tan 70° = cot 20°

⇒ Expression = (1 + sec 20° + tan 20°)(1 − cosec 20° + cot 20°)

⇒ = (1 + 1/cos 20° + sin 20°/cos 20°)(1 − 1/sin 20° + cos 20°/sin 20°)

⇒ = [(cos 20° + 1 + sin 20°)/cos 20°] × [(sin 20° − 1 + cos 20°)/sin 20°]

⇒ = [(sin 20° + cos 20° + 1)(sin 20° + cos 20° − 1)] / (sin 20° × cos 20°)

⇒ Using (a+b)(a−b) = a² − b²: [(sin 20° + cos 20°)² − 1²] / (sin 20° × cos 20°)

⇒ = [sin² 20° + cos² 20° + 2 sin 20° cos 20° − 1] / (sin 20° × cos 20°)

⇒ = [1 + 2 sin 20° cos 20° − 1] / (sin 20° × cos 20°)

⇒ = 2 sin 20° cos 20° / sin 20° cos 20° = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Standard Result

The expression (1 + tan θ + sec θ)(1 + cot θ − cosec θ) always evaluates to 2 for all values of θ where the functions are defined.</p

questions.question: If tan⁴θ + tan²θ = 1 then the value of cos⁴θ + cos²θ is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: tan⁴θ + tan²θ = 1

Factorize: tan²θ(tan²θ + 1) = 1

Using identity 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ: tan²θ × sec²θ = 1

tan²θ = 1 / sec²θ ⇒ tan²θ = cos²θ

Required value: cos⁴θ + cos²θ = (tan²θ)² + tan²θ = tan⁴θ + tan²θ = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** tan⁴θ + tan²θ = 1

**Formula Used:** sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5feb86931f4cb8e92458e2241b544845dc1fb8a22c95c385c5232b7dae05e528.png] 

⇒ tan⁴θ + tan²θ = 1

⇒ tan²θ(tan²θ + 1) = 1

⇒ tan²θ × sec²θ = 1

⇒ (sin²θ / cos²θ) × (1 / cos²θ) = 1

⇒ sin²θ / cos⁴θ = 1

⇒ sin²θ = cos⁴θ

⇒ Now, we need to find cos⁴θ + cos²θ

⇒ Substitute cos⁴θ = sin²θ in the expression:

⇒ sin²θ + cos²θ

⇒ Since sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | 2. 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ | 3. 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Identities

sec θ = 1 / cos θ and cosec θ = 1 / sin θ. Also, tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.

Complementary Angle Properties

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, cos(90° − θ) = sin θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.</p

questions.question: The value of 8(sin⁶θ + cos⁶θ) - 12(sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ) is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Value Substitution Method: Since the expression is independent of θ, substitute a convenient value for θ.

Let θ = 0°

sin 0° = 0 and cos 0° = 1

Expression = 8(0⁶ + 1⁶) − 12(0⁴ + 1⁴)

Expression = 8(1) − 12(1) = 8 − 12 = −4

**∴ The correct answer is −4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 8(sin⁶θ + cos⁶θ) − 12(sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ)

**Formula Used:**

1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

2. a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b)

3. a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1fb239bc0e2fbeefd8adf66b9bee0601909eb62e24807abc1a28d3d517327d4d.png] 

Applying the identities to the powers of sinθ and cosθ:

⇒ sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)² − 2 sin²θ cos²θ

⇒ sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ

⇒ sin⁶θ + cos⁶θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)³ − 3 sin²θ cos²θ (sin²θ + cos²θ)

⇒ sin⁶θ + cos⁶θ = 1 − 3 sin²θ cos²θ

Substitute these into the main expression:

⇒ 8(1 − 3 sin²θ cos²θ) − 12(1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ)

⇒ 8 − 24 sin²θ cos²θ − 12 + 24 sin²θ cos²θ

⇒ 8 − 12 = −4

**∴ The correct answer is −4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identity

The most basic identity is sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, which relates the sine and cosine of any angle.

Power Expansion Rules

Higher even powers of sine and cosine can always be expressed in terms of (sin²θ + cos²θ) and the product (sinθcosθ).

Independence of Variable

When a trigonometric expression results in a constant numerical value across all options, it implies the expression is independent of the angle θ.</p

questions.question: If the angle of elevation of the sun decreases from 45° to 30°, then the length of the shadow of a pillar increases by 60 m. The height of the pillar is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The height of the pillar h = d ÷ (cot θ₂ − cot θ₁), where d is the increase in shadow length.

Here, d = 60 m, θ₁ = 45°, and θ₂ = 30°.

h = 60 ÷ (cot 30° − cot 45°) = 60 ÷ (√3 − 1).

On rationalizing: h = [60 × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)] = 60(√3 + 1) ÷ 2 = 30(√3 + 1).

**∴ The correct answer is 30(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in shadow length (CD) = 60 m

Angle of elevation 1 (θ₁) = 45°

Angle of elevation 2 (θ₂) = 30°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00e13d8cd4fea22c9dd089fcccf072ecb00cb9f901d45a6b42bacb8f2b9746ba.png] 

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base | cot θ = Base / Perpendicular

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the height of the pillar AB be h meters.

⇒ In ▵ABC, cot 45° = BC / AB

⇒ 1 = BC / h ⇒ BC = h

⇒ In ▵ABD, cot 30° = BD / AB

⇒ √3 = BD / h ⇒ BD = h√3

⇒ Increase in shadow = BD − BC = 60 m

⇒ h√3 − h = 60

⇒ h(√3 − 1) = 60

⇒ h = 60 / (√3 − 1)

⇒ h = [60 × (√3 + 1)] / [(√3 − 1) × (√3 + 1)]

⇒ h = [60(√3 + 1)] / (3 − 1)

⇒ h = 60(√3 + 1) / 2

⇒ h = 30(√3 + 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 30(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Height and Distance General Formula

When the angle changes from α to β (α > β) and the shadow increases by distance d, the height h is given by h = d ÷ (cot β − cot α).

Standard Trigonometric Values

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3. Correspondingly, cot 30° = √3, cot 45° = 1, cot 60° = 1/√3.

Angle of Elevation vs Depression

The angle of elevation from an observer's eye to an object above is numerically equal to the angle of depression from the object to the observer's eye due to alternate interior angles.</p

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower, vertically erected in the middle of a paddy field, from two points on a horizontal line through the foot of the tower and opposite side of the tower are given to be α and β (α > β). The height of the tower is h unit. A possible distance (in the same unit) between the points is:

options.text: frac{{h( {tan beta - tan alpha } )}}{{tan alpha tan beta }}

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a tower of height h, if points are on opposite sides with angles α and β:

Distance from foot to first point (d₁) = h × cot α

Distance from foot to second point (d₂) = h × cot β

Total distance between points = d₁ + d₂ = h(cot α + cot β)

**∴ The correct answer is h(cot α + cot β) unit.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the tower = h unit

Angle of elevation from first point (A) = α

Angle of elevation from second point (B) = β

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/981744a5a453bf6bf230aafd85a670dd6c510231e41bb41780172cf31c7f7b78.png] 

In right-angled triangle formed with point A and tower foot F:

⇒ tan α = height / AF = h / AF

⇒ AF = h / tan α = h cot α

In right-angled triangle formed with point B and tower foot F:

⇒ tan β = height / FB = h / FB

⇒ FB = h / tan β = h cot β

Since points A and B are on opposite sides of the tower:

⇒ Distance AB = AF + FB

⇒ Distance AB = h cot α + h cot β

⇒ Distance AB = h(cot α + cot β)

**∴ The correct answer is h(cot α + cot β) unit.**

**__Additional Information__**

Opposite Side vs Same Side Distance

When points are on the opposite side, distance is h(cot α + cot β). If points are on the same side, distance is h|cot α − cot β|.

Trigonometric Ratios in Heights and Distances

The ratio tan θ = Perpendicular/Base is most commonly used. Note that cot θ = 1/tan θ is equivalent to Base/Perpendicular.

Angle of Elevation and α > β

As the point moves closer to the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation increases. Since α > β, point A is closer to the tower than point B.</p

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of an unfinished pillar from a point 150 metres from its base is 30°. The height (in metres) that the pillar must be raised so that its angle of elevation at the same point may be 45°, is (taking √3 = 1.732)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Height to be raised (h) = Distance from base × (tan θ₂ − tan θ₁)

Here, Distance = 150 m, θ₁ = 30°, θ₂ = 45°

h = 150 × (tan 45° − tan 30°) = 150 × (1 − 1/√3)

h = 150 − 150/√3 = 150 − 50√3 = 150 − (50 × 1.732)

h = 150 − 86.6 = 63.4 m

**∴ The correct answer is 63.4 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance from base (BP) = 150 m

Initial angle of elevation (θ₁) = 30°

Final angle of elevation (θ₂) = 45°

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Opposite Side / Adjacent Side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f668d65594a7b5bc7520808ce28c768d406e3566bb2bae851b71137329d78a0f.png] 

Let AB be the initial height of the pillar and BC be the height to be raised.

Total height AC = AB + BC

In ΔABP:

⇒ tan 30° = AB / BP

⇒ 1 / √3 = AB / 150

⇒ AB = 150 / √3 = (150 × √3) / 3 = 50 × 1.732

⇒ AB = 86.6 m

In ΔCBP:

⇒ tan 45° = AC / BP

⇒ 1 = AC / 150

⇒ AC = 150 m

Height to be raised (BC):

⇒ BC = AC − AB

⇒ BC = 150 − 86.6

⇒ BC = 63.4 m

**∴ The correct answer is 63.4 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

For any angle θ in a right triangle: tan θ = Perpendicular / Base, sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, and cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse.

Angle of Elevation

The angle between the horizontal line from the observer and the line of sight to an object above the horizontal level.

Standard Values

Common values used: tan 30° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3 ≈ 1.732.</p
